_draft.rule_lines: Add to .claude/rules/glossary.md '### Terms' (alphabetical position in the first block): 'tool adoption', 'tool exception', 'update channel'. See glossary.md.diff
_draft.why: D-TS6: /tool-adopt reuses 'adopt', already governed twice: 'accept & adopt' ([a] menu option and outcome in managed-file deployment) and 'adoption' (framework adoption, DTCC steps 4-6). The new term names the third meaning and states the other two so no reader conflates them.

tool adoption.definition: The /tool-adopt process that makes a managed tool supported on a platform and environment: an approved preferred method in the tool registry (running /tool-eval when there is none), the registry data the tool support decision tree reads, setup scripts that run the tree, installer and build integration, and verification. Runs after /tool-eval. Not the managed-file [a]dopt choice or its 'accept & adopt' outcome (local content written back to its source), and not framework 'adoption' (mapping a discipline's concepts into the harness).

tool exception.definition: A recorded per-machine decision to keep a non-preferred or unknown-source install of a managed tool instead of replacing it, made with [k]eep in the install-method menu and stored in the dotprofile profile under profiles.<alias>.toolExceptions. While it matches the detected method and path, setup scripts log it as a known exception and do not prompt, update, or post-check that tool.

update channel.definition: The release stream a managed tool's preferred install follows, set per tool in the tool registry (updateChannel): latest-stable (default), lts, pinned-major, pinned-minor, or vendor-auto. Every installer run (aitools install, or aitools sync running the installer) updates the preferred install to its channel's latest and verifies it.

managed tool.old: A CLI tool, dependency, or build tool governed by reference/tool-registry.md. Each gets setup scripts, platform lifecycle tracking, and a corresponding user skill. Standing orders and hooks enforce tool selection.
managed tool.new: A CLI tool, dependency, or build tool with an entry in the tool registry (/tool-registry skill). Each gets setup scripts that run the tool support decision tree, platform and environment lifecycle tracking, and a corresponding user skill. Standing orders and hooks enforce tool selection.
managed tool.why: The JSON registry is canonical since the registries/ consolidation; reference/tool-registry.md is a stale human copy.
